deviation_mechanism: The chirp hypothesis relies on a controlled, monotonic variation in layer thickness to broaden the photonic bandgap smoothly. Unconstrained optimization produced abrupt optical path discontinuities (e.g., candidate 4 layer 5 at 101.05912461266945 nm jumping to layer 6 at 64.85397917780637 nm). These sharp gradients break the cumulative phase-matching condition required for constructive interference in the visible band, scattering coherent energy into higher-order diffraction modes and increasing in-band ripple. The optimizer initially discarded the uniform 75.0 nm starting stack (candidate 1) because it could not satisfy the chirp gradient constraints, and subsequent free-form searches lacked physical regularization, driving the system into locally deep but globally suboptimal interference minima.
